newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee reverses down as traders cash profits.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee reverses down as traders cash profits.

text.p: London coffee prices reversed from their highs on Wednesday as traders and producers cashed in their profits after a steep rally on Tuesday, ignoring technical charts that suggested further gains.

Snubbing the higher opening due, the benchmark May Robusta contract slid to a midday close of $1,603 a tonne, down $40 on the day, exposing the psychological $1,600 which analysts see as key to maintaining the upside momentum.
The drop, after Tuesday's burst to $1,680 a tonne, widened further the arbitrage against New York's Arabica, now around 85 cents a lb.
"They are almost two different markets now," said one trader commenting on the ballooning gap between Robusta and Arabica.
Analysts said soluble coffee producers could be tempted to consider a change in blend towards more use of the cheaper Robusta, but they would be limited in the extent to which they play with flavour.
"There is some scope for that, although it's not massive," said one trader.
The midsession volume reached 3,608 lots. May coffee traded between $1,603 and $1,640, ending at the session's lowest.
Technically, the market should hold its recent strength and make another foray towards $1,700, with a pennant formation in the last month showing a target of $1,800.
